entries.question_en: What are the roles of a BHW?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang mga tungkulin ng isang BHW?
entries.answer_en: Under the UHC Act a BHW is the barangay's Health Education and Promotion Officer (HEPO), and under that umbrella sit three roles described in the DOH BHW Reference Manual. Health Educator: giving people the knowledge to keep their bodies and surroundings healthy, at every stage of life. Community Organizer: keeping communication open between the community and the city or municipal health staff, organising people to take part, and sitting on the barangay planning team for health. Health Service Provider: being the community's first contact, giving simple initial services, guiding people where to go, monitoring health afterwards, and keeping the household records. They are not three separate jobs — an ordinary day usually calls for all three.
entries.answer_fil: Sa ilalim ng UHC Act, ang BHW ang Health Education and Promotion Officer (HEPO) ng barangay, at sa ilalim ng payong na ito ay tatlong tungkuling inilalarawan ng BHW Reference Manual ng DOH. Health Educator: pagbibigay ng kaalaman kung paano panatilihing malusog ang katawan at kapaligiran, sa bawat yugto ng buhay. Community Organizer: pagpapanatili ng komunikasyon sa pagitan ng komunidad at ng health staff ng lungsod o munisipyo, pag-oorganisa ng mga tao para lumahok, at pag-upo sa barangay planning team for health. Health Service Provider: pagiging unang nasasalubong ng pangangailangan, pagbibigay ng paunang serbisyo, paggabay kung saan pupunta, pagsubaybay pagkatapos, at paghawak ng mga talaan ng kabahayan. Hindi ito tatlong magkahiwalay na trabaho — sa ordinaryong araw, madalas gamitin ang tatlo.

entries.question_en: What does HEPO mean, and why is a BHW called one?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang ibig sabihin ng HEPO, at bakit tinatawag na HEPO ang BHW?
entries.answer_en: HEPO stands for Health Education and Promotion Officer. Because the UHC Act of 2019 pushes the health system towards primary care and health promotion, BHWs were designated barangay-level HEPOs — meaning they are expected to carry health information to their communities so people can look after their own health. HEPO is the umbrella name for the whole role; the three roles in the DOH BHW Reference Manual (Health Educator, Community Organizer, Health Service Provider) sit underneath it. To do it, a BHW needs enough knowledge of the barangay's priority health programmes and health problems to share them.
entries.answer_fil: Ang HEPO ay Health Education and Promotion Officer. Dahil itinutulak ng UHC Act of 2019 ang sistemang pangkalusugan tungo sa primary care at health promotion, itinalaga ang mga BHW bilang HEPO sa antas ng barangay — ibig sabihin, inaasahan silang maghatid ng impormasyong pangkalusugan sa kanilang pamayanan upang maalagaan ng mga tao ang sariling kalusugan. Ang HEPO ang pangalan ng buong papel; nasa ilalim nito ang tatlong tungkulin sa BHW Reference Manual ng DOH (Health Educator, Community Organizer, Health Service Provider). Para magawa ito, kailangan ng BHW ng sapat na kaalaman sa mga prayoridad na programa at problemang pangkalusugan ng barangay.

entries.question_en: Why is a BHW's role bigger under the UHC Act?
entries.question_fil: Bakit mas malaki ang tungkulin ng BHW sa ilalim ng UHC Act?
entries.answer_en: Because the UHC Act's direction is primary health care and health promotion, not treatment alone. Asked what their work is, most BHWs answer in terms of services — weighing, immunisation, referral — and that is real work. But UHC expects a bigger part in promoting health in the community: teaching and organising before illness arrives, not only carrying a service to someone already sick. UHC did not add patients; it changed the direction.
entries.answer_fil: Dahil ang direksyon ng UHC Act ay primary health care at health promotion, hindi lamang paggamot. Kapag tinanong kung ano ang trabaho nila, karamihan sa mga BHW ay sumasagot tungkol sa serbisyo — pagtimbang, pagbabakuna, pag-refer — at totoong gawain ang mga iyon. Ngunit inaasahan ng UHC ang mas malaking papel sa pagsulong ng kalusugan sa komunidad: pagtuturo at pag-oorganisa bago pa dumating ang sakit, hindi lamang paghatid ng serbisyo sa may sakit na. Hindi nagdagdag ng pasyente ang UHC; binago nito ang direksyon.

entries.question_en: What does a BHW do as a Health Educator?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang ginagawa ng BHW bilang Health Educator?
entries.answer_en: The Health Educator gives people the knowledge to keep both their bodies and their surroundings healthy — so water, waste, mosquitoes and the cleanliness of where they live are part of it, not just illness. The teaching is continuous rather than a one-off talk, and it prepares people for the illnesses, accidents and risk factors that belong to each stage of life: an infant's risks differ from a teenager's, a pregnant woman's, an elderly person's. It reaches every sector of the community, from children through to the elderly.
entries.answer_fil: Binibigyan ng Health Educator ang mga tao ng kaalaman kung paano panatilihing malusog ang kanilang katawan at ang kanilang kapaligiran — kaya kasama rito ang tubig, basura, lamok, at kalinisan ng tinitirhan, hindi lamang ang sakit. Tuloy-tuloy ang pagtuturo, hindi minsanang usapan, at naghahanda ito sa tao para sa mga sakit, aksidente, at panganib sa bawat yugto ng buhay: iba ang panganib sa sanggol, iba sa kabataan, iba sa buntis, iba sa matanda. Inaabot nito ang bawat sektor ng komunidad, mula sa mga bata hanggang sa mga nakatatanda.

entries.question_en: What does a BHW do as a Community Organizer?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang ginagawa ng BHW bilang Community Organizer?
entries.answer_en: The Community Organizer keeps good relationships and open communication running in two directions — downward to community leaders and members, upward to the city or municipal health staff — so the BHW is the bridge between them. Beyond relationships, the role organises community members and encourages them to take part rather than watch. The BHW is also a member of the barangay planning team for health, where they help community leaders understand the barangay's own health problems and act on them. Under UHC, the Local Investment Plan for Health (LIPH) recognises that barangay contribution to planning, so BHWs are expected to participate in local health planning too.
entries.answer_fil: Pinapanatili ng Community Organizer ang magandang relasyon at bukas na komunikasyon sa dalawang direksyon — pababa sa mga lider at miyembro ng komunidad, pataas sa health staff ng lungsod o munisipyo — kaya ang BHW ang tulay sa pagitan nila. Higit sa relasyon, gawain nitong mag-organisa ng mga miyembro ng komunidad at hikayatin silang lumahok, hindi lamang manood. Miyembro rin ang BHW ng barangay planning team for health, kung saan tinutulungan niya ang mga lider na maintindihan ang sariling problemang pangkalusugan ng barangay at aksyunan ito. Sa ilalim ng UHC, kinikilala ng Local Investment Plan for Health (LIPH) ang kontribusyong ito ng barangay sa pagpaplano, kaya inaasahan ding lumahok ang mga BHW sa lokal na pagpaplanong pangkalusugan.

entries.question_en: What does a BHW do as a Health Service Provider?
entries.question_fil: Ano ang ginagawa ng BHW bilang Health Service Provider?
entries.answer_en: The BHW is part of the city or municipal primary care team and the barangay midwife's partner in delivering services. They are the community's first contact — the frontline — which does not mean treating everything themselves, but being the first to know and guiding the person to where their need can actually be met. They also provide simple initial services: interviewing, taking vital signs, recording, making the household profile, and first aid. Care does not stop at one visit: the BHW monitors people's health over time, which is what keeps care continuous when no doctor is present.
entries.answer_fil: Ang BHW ay bahagi ng primary care team ng lungsod o munisipyo at katuwang ng midwife sa barangay sa paghatid ng serbisyo. Siya ang unang nasasalubong ng pangangailangan — ang frontline — na hindi nangangahulugang siya ang gagamot sa lahat, kundi siya ang unang nakakaalam at siya ang gagabay sa tao kung saan talaga matutugunan ang pangangailangan nito. Nagbibigay din siya ng simple at paunang serbisyo: pakikipanayam, pagsukat ng vital signs, pagtatala, paggawa ng household profile, at paunang lunas. Hindi nagtatapos sa isang pagbisita ang pangangalaga: sinusubaybayan ng BHW ang kalusugan ng mga tao, at ito ang nagpapatuloy sa pangangalaga kahit walang doktor.

entries.question_en: What records and documents is a BHW responsible for?
entries.question_fil: Anong mga talaan at dokumento ang responsibilidad ng BHW?
entries.answer_en: Four kinds. The household profile — a picture of each household in the BHW's assigned area. The master list — a roll of each group in the community: infants, children, pregnant women, people with serious illness, the elderly. The registry — the record of who has already been given a service. And the government, DOH or local government forms the health centre's nurse, midwife or doctor may assign. This is not paperwork for its own sake: these data are what guide health programmes on where to go and what to prioritise, so an inaccurate record means help pointed in the wrong direction. Completing work-related documents is also one of the three TESDA outcomes for this competency.
entries.answer_fil: Apat na uri. Ang household profile — ang larawan ng bawat kabahayan sa nasasakupan ng BHW. Ang master list — ang talaan ng bawat grupo sa komunidad: sanggol, bata, buntis, may malubhang sakit, nakatatanda. Ang registry — ang talaan ng mga nabigyan na ng serbisyo. At ang mga form ng gobyerno, DOH, o lokal na pamahalaan na maaaring ipagawa ng nurse, midwife, o doktor ng health center. Hindi ito papeles para sa papeles: ang mga datos na ito ang gumagabay sa mga programang pangkalusugan kung saan sila pupunta at ano ang uunahin, kaya ang maling talaan ay nangangahulugang maling direksyon ng tulong. Ang pagkumpleto ng mga dokumento sa trabaho ay isa rin sa tatlong TESDA outcome ng competency na ito.

entries.question_en: How do I know which of my roles a situation needs?
entries.question_fil: Paano ko malalaman kung aling tungkulin ang kailangan sa isang sitwasyon?
entries.answer_en: Ask what the situation calls for rather than whether it is your job. If you are giving people knowledge so they can avoid something before it happens, that is Health Educator. If you are bringing people together or connecting the community with the health staff so something can move, that is Community Organizer. If someone's need has arrived and you are meeting it first — measuring, recording, giving initial care, guiding them where to go — that is Health Service Provider. One thing you notice is often the business of all three at once: a household with standing water can be recorded, explained, and raised with the kagawad.
entries.answer_fil: Itanong kung ano ang kailangan ng sitwasyon, hindi kung trabaho mo ba ito. Kung nagbibigay ka ng kaalaman para maiwasan ang isang bagay bago pa mangyari, Health Educator iyon. Kung nagbubuklod ka ng tao o nag-uugnay sa komunidad at sa health staff para may kumilos, Community Organizer iyon. Kung dumating na ang pangangailangan at ikaw ang unang tumutugon — sumusukat, nagtatala, nagbibigay ng paunang alaga, gumagabay kung saan pupunta — Health Service Provider iyon. Ang isang bagay na napansin mo ay kadalasang may kinalaman sa tatlo nang sabay: ang kabahayang may naipong tubig ay maitatala, maipapaliwanag, at maiaakyat sa kagawad.
